messages:
leo: seeing a big spike of 429s on the dedicated pool rdm-dedicated-eu-1 since ~09:22 UTC. Users report latency >3s for short prompts. Logs show `throttled_by_kv_cache`. tagging support.
maya: thanks — can you paste a few request ids + a short log snippet? any chance this correlates with long-context jobs or a deploy? :eyes:
leo: sample logs attached below
```
2026-02-16T09:22:11Z req=01E7X2 id=7890 status=429 throttle_reason=kv_cache_pressure kv_cache_evictions=132 kv_cache_bytes=48.1GB kv_cache_limit=50GB mem_fragmentation=0.14
2026-02-16T09:25:04Z req=01E7X3 id=7891 status=200 latency_ms=3200 model=mistral-32k stream=true
2026-02-16T09:28:30Z req=01E7X4 id=7892 status=429 throttle_reason=kv_cache_pressure evictions/sec=110
```
leo: also saw autoscaler not spin up even though tail latencies rose. pool reports GPU mem ~78%, worker host mem post-alloc ~92%.
sam: that's a lot of eviction churn. which model variants are on that pool? any partner running very long contexts?
leo: mostly mistral-7b-32k, but one partner started running reranker batch jobs with ~200k token contexts via streaming. they ramped up ~09:15.
jordan: autoscaler logic currently scales on GPU metrics (util + mem) and request queue depth, not on host-side KV cache pressure. the KV cache lives on host memory per worker, so heavy long-context jobs can exhaust cache and cause eviction which triggers request-level throttles. can you paste metrics for kv_cache_bytes + evictions?
leo: metrics (15m window):
```
kv_cache_bytes: 48.1GB (limit 50GB)
evictions/sec: 120
throttle_count: 342
gpu_mem_used: 78%
host_mem_used: 92%
```
maya: escalating to Eng-Platform + SRE. opening ticket INF-3974. @jordan can you triage? in the meantime we can either bump the per-tenant kv_cache_size or pin that partner to a separate larger pool.
jordan: i'll take a look. quick repro I used locally:
```
curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Context-Length: 200000" \
  -d '{"model":"mistral-7b-32k","input":"<long_prompt>"}'
# results in repeated cache insert ops and then evictions and a 429:
# {"error":"throttled_by_kv_cache","code":429}
```
jordan: short-term workarounds: 1) throttle admission for long-context requests for that tenant; 2) increase `kv_cache_size_bytes` for their pool; 3) move their jobs to a dedicated larger pool. longer-term: change autoscaler to consider kv_cache_pressure metric or migrate KV store to reserved shared memory with compaction.
sam: agree on admission control. we should add a light-weight per-tenant check: if kv_cache_fill_ratio > 0.8 deny/queue long-context requests. i've got a branch to enforce admission checks on canary.
leo: customer is okay with soft throttling if it avoids whole-pool impact. they want repro steps and timeline for fixes.
maya: added timeline and notes to INF-3974, requested maintenance window. set temporary alert: kv_cache_evictions > 50/min -> page oncall. incident-bot: created ticket INF-3974 by maya.
incident-bot: Ticket INF-3974 created: "Dedicated pool kv-cache evictions causing throttling" assigned to eng-platform.
jordan: initial root-cause hypothesis: long-context streaming jobs create many unique prefix keys, LRU churn multiplies, plus large allocations cause host heap fragmentation so available contiguous cache decreases leading to more evictions even below absolute limit. remediation candidates: compactible cache allocator, periodic compaction on idle, increase host-reserved memory for cache, or change admission to coalesce streaming keys.
sam: i'll run heap profiler on the affected worker images and check jemalloc fragmentation metrics + per-worker malloc arenas.
leo: roughly ETA for an actionable mitigation?
jordan: admission-control canary in ~6h, will throttle long-context admissions. config increase/pool pinning we can do immediately for that tenant. full allocator/compaction work will be 1-2 sprints. i'll update INF-3974 with patch links and timeline.
maya: thanks all — will keep customer updated. tagging @support-runbooks to add a KB article for "kv-cache pressure" and suggested mitigations.
leo: appreciated. please post when canary is live.
